 WP(C) NO. 5029 OF 2011 ..2..
 JUDGMENT
The 1st petitioner is a registered Association and its members, including the 2nd petitioner, are engaged in the business of sale of food articles within the State.

They have filed this writ petition challenging schedule I and II to the Kerala Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 2007 which prescribes much larger fees than what is prescribed under the Kerala Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1957 towards licence fee and renewal fee.

entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Kerala Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1957
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
They have also challenged Ext.P3 Government Order GO.(MS)No.15/2008/H&FWD dated 09.01.2009 by which the imposition of licence fee under the 2007 Rules was frozen on condition that the applicants pay 25 times of the pre-existing licence fee and on further condition that the applicants file undertaking that they will pay the balance amount of WP(C) NO. 5029 OF 2011 ..3..
fees, if any, subject to the final judgment in W.P.(C) No. 12727/2007 and connected cases.

2. The petitioners have also relied on the interim orders in W.P.(C) No.11502/2010 and connected cases and this Court has passed a similar interim order dated 17.02.2011 in this writ petition staying the operation and enforcement of the schedules of the Kerala Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 2007 and Ext.P3 Government Order and collection of payments as per the said schedules and the Government Order.

entities.text: Kerala Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 2007
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It was also ordered that the renewal, if any made, will be subject to further orders to be passed in the writ petition.

3. When this writ petition was taken up for consideration today, it is submitted that the batch of writ petitions referred to in this writ petition and in Ext.P3 Government order have been disposed of by Judgment dated 10.03.2017 reported in Palghat WP(C) NO. 5029 OF 2011 ..4..
Chamber of Commerce and others v. State of Kerala and others (2017 (2) KHC 831: 2017 (2) KLT 696: 2017 (2) KLJ 887) holding that Kerala Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 2007 are in order and that it has been issued and notified within the powers available to Government and further directing the Government to take appropriate decision regarding the collection of differential licence fee payable by the petitioners therein who had remitted such licence fee in terms of interim orders of the Court.

4. In the light of the decision taken by this Court in Palghat Chamber of Commerce (supra) the reliefs sought for by the petitioners in the writ petition cannot be granted and this writ petition stands disposed of with the direction that the Government shall take a decision regarding the collection of differential licence fee payable by the members of the 1st petitioner Association, in tune Kerala Merchants Union & Another vs State Of Kerala And Another on 22 July, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30875710/

respect of the petitioners in the batch of writ petitions referred to above.
